title: Best Beaches in Kerala: From Varkala and Kovalam to the Malabar Coast
seoTitle: Best Beaches in Kerala: Varkala, Kovalam to Malabar | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: The best beaches in Kerala, from Varkala's cliffs and Kovalam's lighthouse to Marari, Cherai, Kappad, the Muzhappilangad drive-in beach and Bekal, with the season.
description: A guide to the best beaches in Kerala, south to north: Kovalam, Poovar and Varkala near Thiruvananthapuram, Marari and Alappuzha near the backwaters, Cherai and Fort Kochi, Kappad near Kozhikode, and Muzhappilangad, Payyambalam, Chal and Bekal on the Malabar coast, with seasons and sea-safety rules.
dek: Kerala's 580-odd km of coast pairs beaches with backwaters, Ayurveda and Malabar food. Here is how its best beaches compare, from south to north.

intro: Kerala's coastline runs for around 580 km along the Arabian Sea, from the Tamil Nadu border near Thiruvananthapuram to Karnataka beyond Kasaragod. The beaches in the south, around Kovalam and Varkala, are the most developed, with resorts, Ayurveda centres and cafes. The central coast pairs quiet beaches such as Marari with the backwaters of Alappuzha and Kochi, and the north, the old Malabar coast, has long, uncrowded beaches, forts and a drive-in beach.

Kerala's sea is rough for much of the south-west monsoon, from about June to August, and swimming is unsafe then. This guide goes from south to north. For backwaters, hills and wildlife, see things to do in Kerala.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in Kerala are Varkala for its red cliffs and cafes, Kovalam for its lighthouse beach and Ayurveda resorts, Marari for a quiet village beach near Alappuzha, Cherai near Kochi, Kappad near Kozhikode, and Muzhappilangad, Payyambalam, Chal and Bekal in north Kerala. Go from October to March. Swimming is unsafe in the monsoon, and some beaches have strong currents all year.
takeaways: Varkala and Kovalam, near Thiruvananthapuram, are Kerala's most popular beach towns.
Marari and Cherai combine quiet beaches with the backwaters of Alappuzha and Kochi.
Kappad (Kozhikode) and Chal (Kannur) hold Blue Flag certification.
Muzhappilangad near Thalassery is a drive-in beach where cars can run on the firm sand.
Swim only in lifeguarded zones; the monsoon (June to August) is not a beach season.

items.name: Varkala
body: Varkala's beach lies below red laterite cliffs, with a clifftop walkway lined with cafes and guesthouses. Papanasam, the main beach, is also a place of Hindu rites near the Janardana Swamy temple, so dress respectfully there. Surf schools run lessons in season, and quieter beaches such as Odayam and the Black Beach lie north.

facts.Good to know: Currents can be strong; stay in lifeguarded zones

image.alt: Varkala's red cliffs above the beach
image.caption: Varkala

items.name: Kovalam
body: About 16 km from Thiruvananthapuram, Kovalam has three adjoining crescent beaches: Lighthouse beach, the busiest, below the red-and-white lighthouse; Hawa beach; and Samudra beach to the north. Ayurveda centres and resorts line the headlands.

items.name: Poovar
body: South of Kovalam, where the Neyyar river meets the sea, a golden sandbar separates the estuary from the ocean. It is reached by boat through mangroves, often from resorts that line the backwaters.

items.name: Marari
body: Mararikulam, near Alappuzha, is a fishing-village beach with a handful of homestays and resorts, far quieter than Kovalam or Varkala. It pairs naturally with a houseboat trip.

items.name: Alappuzha beach
body: Alappuzha's town beach, with its old pier and lighthouse, is a place for a sunset walk rather than swimming.

facts.Best for: An evening before or after a houseboat

items.name: Cherai and Fort Kochi
body: Cherai, on Vypeen island north of Kochi, has the sea on one side and backwaters on the other. Fort Kochi's beach is for walks and watching the Chinese fishing nets, not swimming.

items.name: Kappad
body: Near Kozhikode, Kappad is associated with the landing of Vasco da Gama in 1498, marked by a memorial stone, and holds Blue Flag certification.

items.name: Muzhappilangad
body: About 7 km from Thalassery, this long beach has firm sand that visitors can drive on for around 4 km, with Dharmadam island just offshore. Follow the posted rules on where and when driving is allowed.

facts.Good to know: Drive slowly; keep off at high tide

items.name: Payyambalam and Chal
body: Kannur's long town beach, Payyambalam, is popular at sunset. Chal beach, also near Kannur, has Blue Flag certification.

items.name: Bekal and Kappil
body: Bekal Fort, a large laterite fort on a headland, overlooks beaches on both sides; Kappil beach, nearby, is quiet and backed by a backwater.

sections.heading: Planning a Kerala beach trip
list: Thiruvananthapuram airport is closest to Kovalam, Poovar and Varkala; Kochi and Kozhikode serve central and north Kerala; Kannur has its own airport.
Varkala and Kovalam are about 50 km apart; combine them in four to five days.
A classic route is Kochi, the backwaters at Alappuzha with a night at Marari, then Varkala or Kovalam.
North Kerala combines well with theyyam season, roughly October to May.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Kerala beaches can have strong currents and steep drops close to shore; lifeguards at Kovalam and Varkala post warning flags.
Do not climb down the Varkala cliffs except by the marked steps; the edges crumble.
Swimming is unsafe in the monsoon, from about June to August.
At Muzhappilangad, drive slowly, keep away from the water's edge and follow local rules.
Dress modestly at Papanasam, where religious rites take place.
packing: An umbrella or rain jacket in shoulder months

faqs.q: Which is the best beach in Kerala?
faqs.a: Varkala for cliffs and cafes and Kovalam for its lighthouse beach and resorts are the most popular. Marari and Cherai are quieter.

faqs.q: Which Kerala beach is best for families?
faqs.a: Kovalam, Cherai and Payyambalam, which have lifeguards in season and easy facilities.

faqs.q: Can you swim in Kerala beaches?
faqs.a: In lifeguarded zones in the dry season, yes. The sea is rough and unsafe in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Which beach in Kerala allows driving?
faqs.a: Muzhappilangad near Thalassery, a drive-in beach of about 4 km.
